headline: High-risk filesystem and MCP overlap in Gemini CLI can drive prompt injection, leakage, and action cascades when paired with a LangChain4j-based workflow.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Gemini CLI ingests repo files, user directories, stdin/stdout, and user-approved MCP tools; that creates a plausible instruction-injection path if langchain4j passes untrusted content through prompts or files. langchain4j itself has no documented isolation or provenance controls here, so the interaction is inferred rather than directly evidenced.
conditions: IF langchain4j forwards Gemini CLI output or shared files into prompts without sanitization, injection is possible.
IF a user-configured MCP server returns attacker-controlled text, Gemini CLI may treat it as instructions.
mitigations: Disable MCP servers not needed for the task.
Route untrusted text through a fixed sanitizer before prompting.
Use separate workspaces for each agent.
Require explicit human review before executing tool-derived instructions.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Gemini CLI can read and write local files and has broad network egress, while langchain4j is a framework that may be embedded in apps handling the same workspace. Shared files or prompts can therefore leak source code or shell environment data from Gemini into downstream outputs; langchain4j's own network behavior is not documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same directory tree, file contents can flow from Gemini CLI into langchain4j prompts.
IF the embedding application logs prompts or responses, source code or shell environment data may be retained.
mitigations: Separate sensitive and non-sensitive workspaces.
Redact secrets before passing files between agents.
Turn off verbose prompt/response logging.
Use per-agent credentials and API keys.
Restrict Gemini CLI to least-privilege directories.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Gemini CLI can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; the pair shares state via filesystem and git only. If langchain4j is embedded in a companion app that also writes the same repo or git metadata, concurrent writes can collide and corrupt state. Because langchain4j's write scope is undocumented, uncertainty pushes this to high rather than medium.
conditions: IF langchain4j-backed code writes to the same repository or working tree as Gemini CLI, git or file conflicts can occur.
IF both agents mutate shared files without locking, last-writer-wins corruption is possible.
mitigations: Serialize writes with a single lock file.
Assign separate branches or clones per agent.
Disable automatic git commits during parallel runs.
Use a staging directory for generated artifacts.
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency checks around shared writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Gemini CLI can generate code, shell actions, and file edits; langchain4j commonly acts as an orchestration layer that may consume those outputs. If the downstream app treats Gemini output as authoritative, mistakes can cascade into incorrect support actions or code changes. The lack of direct pairwise evidence keeps this below high.
conditions: IF langchain4j uses Gemini CLI output as a final answer without verification, errors can propagate.
IF downstream automation acts on generated text, a mistaken instruction can trigger an incorrect action.
mitigations: Add a verification step before acting on model output.
Require citations or structured schemas for generated facts.
Keep human approval for any external action.
Log and diff all generated changes before applying them.
Use a second model to cross-check critical outputs.

E_compliance.rationale: Gemini CLI handles source code, files in cwd, and shell environment data, but langchain4j's profile does not document any regulated-data handling or residency mismatch. With only one side showing sensitive local data and no evidence of a compliance breach path, the risk is limited to documented gaps rather than a clear violation.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in the shared workspace, Gemini CLI may process it locally.
IF the embedding application routes that data to a non-compliant backend, a policy mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace.
Confirm backend residency and retention settings.
Use separate environments for regulated and unregulated tasks.
Document data-handling responsibilities for the embedding app.
